catalog_locator: Ch. 2 Phonology, section 2.5 Stress (pp. 30-34: 2.5.1 Segmental conditioning of stress placement; 2.5.2 Suprasegmental conditioning of stress placement) and se…
catalog_quote: Stress occurs basically on the last syllable of Karo words. Less frequently, it occurs on penultimate syllables. These occurrences are predictable in terms of segmental and suprasegmental factors. ... From the segmental point of view, stress can be predicted by the onset of the last syllable: if it is a voiced stop consonant, /b/, /r/ or /g/, then the stress shifts one syllable to the left. /yaba/ ['yaba] 'rodent (sp.)' ... /aoro/ [a'oro] 'parrot' ... /macirup/ [ma'c:irup] 'bird (sp.)' ... If the onset of the last syllable is of any other kind rather than /b/, /r/ or /g/ then the stress falls on the last syllable. /peon/ [pe'odn] 'skin' ... /kuru?cu/ [kuru?'cu] 'saliva' ... /kiriwep/ [kiri'wep] 'butterfly' ... new_statements.quote: A ocorrência do acento no Karo é previsível, sendo condicionada por três fatores fonológicos distintos: a) pelo tom; b) pela nasalidade; c) pela qualidade do fonema que inicia a última sílaba das palavras. Esses fatores determinam a posição do acento nas palavras através das seguintes regras, estabelecidas em ordem hierárquica: 1) São acentuadas todas as sílabas com tom alto; [...] 2) Se não há tom alto, acentua-se a sílaba com vogal nasal; [...] 3) Se não há tom alto nem vogal nasal, acentua-se a penúltima sílaba se esta preceder /b/, /r/ ou /g/; [...] 4) Nos demais casos é acentuada a última sílaba; (pp. 64-66)
new_statements.translation: The occurrence of stress in Karo is predictable, being conditioned by three distinct phonological factors: a) tone; b) nasality; c) the quality of the phoneme that begins the last syllable of words. These factors determine the position of stress in words through the following rules, established in hierarchical order: 1) All syllables with high tone are stressed; 2) If there is no high tone, the syllable with a nasal vowel is stressed; 3) If there is neither high tone nor nasal vowel, the penultimate syllable is stressed if it precedes /b/, /r/ or /g/; 4) In the remaining cases the last syllable is stressed.
new_statements.citation: Gabas and Jr. and Nilson (1989). Estudo fonológico da língua karo (Arara de Rondônia). Univ. Estadual. Universidade Estadual de Campinas. vi+85 pp.
new_statements.locator: Chapter 6 'Padrão acentual', pp. 64-67 (PDF pages 70-73); exceptions p. 67 (PDF 73); tone/stress co-occurrence ch. 7 pp. 68-69 (PDF 74-75); summary in Resumo (PDF 3)
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog lists Karo with an empty rule and there are no existing stress statements; this work supplies the placement rule. If the catalog wants a single stress label, the work supports 'predictable; default final, with high-tone and nasal-vowel syllables attracting stress and penultimate stress before a final syllable in /b, r, g/' — i.e. a tone language with a stress statement, not a plain fixed: final syllable language.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Karo has lexical tone (two contrastive tonemes, high and low, p. 69) and predictable stress ('acento de intensidade'). Stress placement is a ranked hierarchy: (1) any high-tone syllable is stressed; (2) otherwise the syllable with a nasal vowel; (3) otherwise the penult when the final syllable begins with /b/, /r/ or /g/ (e.g. /pibe/ ['pibe] 'foot', /yaba/ ['yaba] 'paca', /motogo/ [mo'togo]); (4) otherwise the final syllable (e.g. /ma?pe/ [ma?'pe] 'gourd', /paramit/ [para'mit] 'spider', /mani/ [ma'ni] 'manioc'). So the default, in the absence of high tone, nasal vowels and a voiced-stop/flap onset on the last syllable, is final stress. Ch. 7 adds that mid and high tones co-occur with stress and low tone never occurs on a stressed syllable; the mid tone is the realization of the low toneme under stress (p. 68-69).
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary stress is described. The work states that mid and high tones occur in sequence only 'em palavras complexas, portadoras de dois ou mais acentos' (in complex [polymorphemic] words, bearing two or more stresses), p. 68, so multimorphemic words may carry more than one stress, but no primary/secondary distinction is made.
new_statements.exceptions: p. 67: 'Há, entretanto, um grupo de palavras do corpus cuja ocorrência do acento não se enquadra entre as regras estabelecidas anteriormente. São elas: (651) /korem/ [ko'rɛbm] também; (652) /pagon/ [pa'gɔdn] ?; (653) /acibe/ [ači'bɛ] raiz' — three corpus words whose stress does not follow the rules (all stressed on the final syllable although rule 3 would predict the penult, since the last syllable begins with /r/, /g/, /b/).
new_statements.identity_note: The work describes the Karo of Rondônia (also called Arara de Rondônia), Ramarama branch of the Tupi stock, based on 1987-1989 fieldwork with Arara speakers (cacique Pedro Agamenon; informants Mário Jorge, Carlos, Chiquito and Manoel, per the acknowledgements). No other dialect or variety is distinguished.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim in the held 1999 UCSB reference grammar at the stated locator (sec. 2.5, printed pp. 30-34, PDF pp. 46-50). That grammar is the fullest and latest description of Karo and every Glottolog descriptive reference is by the same author; the earlier phonology monograph (1989 MA, downloaded now to gives the identical analysis as an ordered rule hierarchy (high tone > nasal vowel > penult if final onset /b r g/ > final), so the 'segmental' (onset-conditioned, right-edge, with tone/nasality override and a listed set of lexical exceptions) coding stands. No instrumental study located
